COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
SA No. 74 of 2025
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. V.B.S. Negi and Mr. M.S. Tyagi, learned Sr. 
Advocates assisted by Ms. Asmeen Wilson, learned 
counsel for the appellant.
2. The instant second appeal is preferred against the 
judgment and order dated 04.04.2025 passed by 1st
Addl. District Judge, Dehradun in Civil Appeal No. 83 
of 2022 (Guman Singh and others Vs. Karam Chand 
and others) and judgment and decree dated 11.07.2022 
passed by Civil Judge, Dehradun in O.S. No. 45 of 1995 
(Guman Singh and others Vs. Karam Chand and 
others).
3. The suit was filed by the appellant / plaintiff for 
cancellation of the sale deed on the ground that same 
was executed on the basis of forged and unregistered 
power of attorney. 
4. It is argued by Mr. M.S. Tyagi, learned Sr. 
Advocate for the appellant that while dismissing the 
suit the trial court has not examined whether power of 
attorney has to be registered or not before execution of 
the sale deed. 
5. Being aggrieved with the judgment and decree 
passed by the Trial Court, appellant preferred first 
appeal, that too was dismissed. Now, the instant 
second appeal has been filed. The instant second 
appeal is admitted on the following substantial 
question of law:
 “a. Whether both the learned courts while 
passing the impugned judgments and decrees lost 
sight of the fact that impugned sale deed, has been 
executed on the strength of an unregistered forged 
and fabricated alleged power of attorney and the 
execution of which has been denied by the plaintiff 
no. 1 (now dead) while deposing before the learned 
trial court and the respondents failed to prove the 
same by cogent evidence. 
 b. Whether both the learned courts wrongly 
shifted the burden of proof on the plaintiff and 
wrongly interpreted the provisions of Section 101 and 
103 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 while passing  the impugned judgments and decrees specially when 
the appellant / plaintiff specifically denied the 
execution of alleged power of attorney in favour of 
defendant no. 2.?” 
6. Issue notice to the respondents.
7. Steps be taken within a week.
8. Summon the trial court record. 
9. List after service report along with SA No. 75 of 
2025.
10. In the meantime, both the parties are directed to 
maintain status quo, over the property in question with 
a further rider that they will not create any third party 
interest.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 16.09.2025
SKS

Guman Singh Rawat ........Appellant

Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. V.B.S. Negi, Senior Advocate 
assisted by Azmeen Wason, Advocate holding 
brief of Mr. Ankush Negi, Advocate for the 
appellant.
Mr. Yashpal Singh, Advocate for the 
respondent no.2/1. 
Heard.
By way of the Miscellaneous 
Application, IA No.3 of 2025, the appellant 
proposes to place on record the decree dated 
16.04.2025, passed in the second appeal.
It is allowed. 
The Miscellaneous Application, IA No.3 
of 2025, stands disposed of, accordingly. 
Heard on the Impleadment Applicatoin, 
IA No.4 of 2026.
This application has been filed by the 
appellant Arun Kumar Gupta for his 
impleadment as respondent no.1/1 on the 
ground that his father late Karam Chand was 
respondent no.1 in the instant appeal.
Interestingly, before the IA No.4 of 2026 
filed by the appellant Arun Kumar Gupta 
could be decided, the appellant also filed IA 
No.5 of 2026 for the same direction that Arun 
Kumar Gupta may be impleaded as 
respondent no.1/1.
The appellant himself has filed the  application. There is none to object to it. Both 
the applications, IA No.4 of 2026 and IA No.5 
of 2026, are allowed.
Let Arun Kumar Gupta be impleaded as 
respondent no.1/1. He is already 
represented. 
Let the amended memo of parties be 
filed within a week. 
The instant appeal has already been 
admitted and the substantial questions of 
law were framed on 16.09.2025.
Respondent no.3 has yet not been 
served. 
Issue fresh notices to the respondent 
no.3, returnable within six weeks. 
Steps to be taken within a week. 
List this matter on 03.09.2026. 
 (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
10.07.2026
